title: Growth velocity peaks and falls because surface resistance suddenly increases

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Growth velocity peaks and falls because surface resistance suddenly increases

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The abrupt change from increasing to decreasing growth velocity is more likely due to a sudden increase of resistance, such as the formation of a comparatively firm skin during histological differentiation, than to a decline of internal growth forces; the later slowing reflects waning growth forces against rising superficial resistance.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. III: The Rate of Growth

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: I take it that the sudden arrest of velocity is much more likely to be due to a sudden increase of resistance than to a sudden diminution of internal energies: in other words, I suspect that it is coincident with some notable event of histological differentiation, such as the rapid formation of a comparatively firm skin

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter III, “The Rate of Growth”; topic “Conclusion and summary”. Scope: growing organisms generally, including regenerating tissues

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch03-34: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.40

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The rival mechanisms imply different synchronized trajectories, so the claim is testable in principle. However, current public datasets generally do not combine mechanics, histology, and growth at the required temporal resolution.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Synchronously measure growth velocity, surface stiffness or skin formation, and internal growth-driving pressure through the velocity peak. Support requires the velocity break to follow an abrupt resistance increase while internal drive remains stable; a preceding drop in drive would favor the rival.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Histological differentiation and slowing are temporally correlated confounders.

The claim spans organisms with different growth mechanics.

Existing images rarely include surface resistance and internal driving force.

fields.value:

operationalizability: 0.55

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim is a causal timing statement: the velocity peak is a sudden rise in superficial resistance rather than a drop in internal drive. Growth curves exist, and histology exists, but the paired mechanical variables do not, in an open archive or as a compilable series. Coincidence of skin differentiation with slower growth would not separate the two sides of the proposed conflict.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: At the age when growth velocity switches from rising to falling, measure surface stiffness or skin resistance and an estimate of internal driving force. A step up in resistance at that age, with driving force still high, would support the claim; a falling driving force at constant resistance would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Histological differentiation coincides with many changes besides a firmer skin.

Growth curves are not paired with time-resolved tissue stiffness.

Internal growth force is not a standard archived variable.
